Purchases of property and equipment were $74.4 million in 2025 and $72.5 million in 2024. Purchase of property and equipment for 2025 included $9.7 million of capital expenditures related to damages from natural disasters. Property and equipment are depreciated on a straight-line basis over their useful lives, which are based on management’s estimates of the period over which the assets provide a benefit to the Company. The useful lives are estimated based on historical experience with similar assets as well as other information regarding condition and utility of the assets. Our asset useful lives are generally five to ten years for restaurant, commissary, and other equipment, twenty to forty years for buildings and improvements, and five years for technology and capitalized software. Leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of their estimated useful lives or the term of the respective lease, including the first renewal period (generally five to ten years).

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Approximately 8.5% of our 2025 revenues, 8.5% of our 2024 revenues and 7.4% of our 2023 revenues were derived from these International operations.
No single external customer accounted for 10% or more of our total revenues.
We are dependent on a sole supplier for all of our cheese made from mozzarella domestically and substantially all of our cheese internationally.
We also depend on a sole source for our supply of garlic sauce and we source other key ingredients, including meat products, from a limited number of suppliers.

For a discussion of the related risks, see “Item 1A—Risk Factors—Company Risks—Increase in ingredient and other operating costs, including those caused by weather, climate change and food safety, could adversely affect our results of operations,” “—Our dependence on a sole supplier or a limited number of suppliers for some ingredients and other supplies could result in disruptions to our business,” and “—Changes in purchasing practices by our Domestic franchisees, or prolonged disruptions in our QC Center operations, could harm our commissary business.”
We rely on our Domestic and International suppliers, as do our franchisees, to provide quality ingredients and to comply with applicable laws and industry standards.
Our results depend upon our ability to differentiate our brand and our reputation for quality.
Our success significantly relies on the financial success and cooperation of our franchisees, yet we have limited influence over their operations.

Our success also increasingly depends on the willingness and ability of our franchisees to remain aligned with us on current and future operating, promotional and marketing plans, including favorable support of our Domestic system to approve certain marketing initiatives, products, and national promotions.
We rely on a variety of direct and indirect marketing techniques, including email, text messages, push notifications, social media, behavioral advertising, and postal mailings.
Our business depends on the proper allocation of our human capital and our ability to attract and retain talented management and other key employees.

We rely on information technology to operate our businesses and enhance our competitiveness, and any failure to invest in or adapt to technological developments or industry trends could harm our business.
Our ability to efficiently and effectively manage our business depends on the reliability and capacity of these technology systems.

We rely on our International franchisees to maintain their own point-of-sale, mobile applications, and online ordering systems, which are often purchased from third-party vendors, potentially exposing International franchisees to more operational risk, including cybersecurity and data privacy risks and governmental regulation compliance risks.
The success of our business depends on the effectiveness of our marketing and promotional plans, including local and regional market efforts with our franchisees.
Our growth strategy depends on our and our franchisees’ ability to open new restaurants and to operate them on a profitable basis.
Accordingly, our profitability significantly depends upon royalty revenues from franchisees.
Our dependence on a sole supplier or a limited number of suppliers for some ingredients and other supplies could result in disruptions to our business.
We also depend on a sole source for our supply of garlic sauce, which constitutes a small percentage of our purchased food items.
While we have no other sole sources of supply for key ingredients or menu items, we do source other key ingredients from a limited number of suppliers.
Insolvency of key suppliers could also cause similar business interruptions and negatively impact our business.

We rely on third parties for certain business processes and services, and failure or inability of such third-party vendors to perform subjects us to risks, including business disruption and increased costs.
We depend on the performance of suppliers, aggregators and other third parties in our business operations.
In some cases, we rely on a relatively small number of third-party vendors to support these critical business processes and services.

Our ability to fund our expenses and to pay principal of and interest on our indebtedness when due thus depends on our future performance, which will be affected by financial, business, economic and other factors.
We depend on the Papa John’s brand name and rely on a combination of trademarks, service marks, copyrights, trade secrets and similar intellectual property rights to protect and promote our brand.

We believe the success of our business depends on our continued ability to exclusively use our existing marks to increase brand awareness and further develop our brand, both domestically and internationally.
